business: BusinessOS (a WhatsApp-native AI assistant that captures a shop's orders and keeps its udhaar book)
target: Owners of small neighbourhood shops in India (kirana and similar) who take dozens of orders a day by phone call and WhatsApp and keep udhaar in a paper diary
where: Dense urban and semi-urban neighbourhoods in India (guess: Hindi-speaking north and west India first)

behaviours.name: Paper-diary loyalist
behaviours.how: Has kept the udhaar diary for years and trusts it more than any phone.

behaviours.name: WhatsApp-heavy
behaviours.how: Takes most orders on WhatsApp text and voice notes already, comfortable with the phone.

behaviours.name: Phone-call ordering
behaviours.how: Most customers just call; rarely types anything.

behaviours.name: Tried a ledger app
behaviours.how: Installed Khatabook or OkCredit once and stopped updating it.

behaviours.name: Family-run, son or daughter handles the phone
behaviours.how: A younger family member manages apps; the owner decides.

behaviours.name: Cost-sensitive skeptic
behaviours.how: Will not pay for anything that is not clearly putting rupees back in the till.

objections: I don't trust an app or AI with my customers' udhaar details
Half my orders come by call, so this misses them
Another thing to learn and keep up every day
What if it writes the wrong order and I lose a customer's trust?
Chasing udhaar through a bot will upset my regulars
What is the catch if it is free?
Will it understand my Hindi, my regional words and my item names?
habits: you take orders by call and WhatsApp voice note while serving customers at the counter
you write udhaar in a paper diary at the end of the day
you keep stock in your head and order from the same two or three vendors
you already use UPI QR at the counter
